svg.text: FIG 11 — OFFLINE-FIRST RURAL ARCHITECTURE & CELLULAR RESILIENCE
Guaranteed persistence during extended Himalayan or forest network blackouts
STATE A: NORMAL ONLINE UPLINK
Continuous Data Ingestion
1. Field LoRa packet arrives at gateway (SX1262 SPI).
2. Gateway decodes 40-byte binary frame into telemetry dict.
3. Writes immediately to local SQLite WAL database.
4. Real-time HTTPS POST to cloud server (/api/v1/telemetry).
5. Cloud acknowledges; record tagged 'SYNCED'.
LIVE CLOUD TELEMETRY
STATE B: RURAL NETWORK OUTAGE (CELLULAR DOWN)
Zero Data Loss Local Spooling
1. Cloud uplink times out (HTTP 504 / network unreachable).
2. Gateway continues logging to local SQLite WAL queue.
3. 32 GB MicroSD holds up to 18 months of continuous telemetry.
4. Background sync worker checks uplink every 60 seconds.
5. Upon reconnection: batches spool up chronologically.
LOCAL WAL BUFFERING (100% PERSISTENT)
Rural Suitability Verification:

In remote apicultural regions across Jammu & Kashmir, Western Ghats, and the North East, cellular connectivity is intermittent. Honey Chain ensures beekeepers never lose historical comb production or harvest records during monsoon or infrastructure outages.
